does_not_discharge: runtime-design-review. Judging the final bytes never establishes that the design was independently challenged before anyone wrote them, and this obligation cannot be satisfied in advance: a review performed before the final head existed did not review this change. Neither obligation discharges the other and each must be recorded against the head it actually read.
source: data/runtime-reviewer-role-qualification/report.md:65-96,126-142,386 (home-private). The predicate set is shared with the design role because the qualification source derived ONE read-only reviewer floor; what differs is the artifact, the obligation point, and the pinned-head requirement below.
requires_pinned_head_why: A review of another head or of stale bytes does not satisfy this obligation. The reviewed head is therefore a required INPUT to the assignment decision rather than something recorded afterwards, and an assignment naming no head is refused rather than assumed to mean the current one - which is the only reading under which the head could silently change between the review and the landing.
independence_note: Identical to the design role's, and stated here rather than referenced because a role file is read on its own by the interpreter and a cross-reference would make one of the two roles unreadable in isolation. The dimension NAMES remain owned by bin/fm-independence-lib.sh.
